chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed a chick while he was in Ihram, outside the Haram (Sanctuary). He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a lamb, and there is no evaluation upon him because he is not inside the Haram.'

key_terms.حَمَل: A lamb (specific type of animal expiation)
key_terms.قِيمَة: Valuation/Evaluation of the specific item killed
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a bird outside the Haram for one in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the penalty for killing game inside versus outside the Haram, establishing that a lamb (hal) is due for a chick killed outside, without the need for valuation (qimah). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the severity of the penalty is tied to the sanctity of the specific location, reflecting the principle that the Haram's boundaries carry unique legal weight in Ihram regulations. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the graduated nature of fidya (expiation) in Shia fiqh.
